html:
Novo Brdo is a hill town in eastern Kosovo whose mines made it the biggest source of silver in the Balkans in the 1300s and 1400s. Its fortress ruins still stand above the village.

Saxon miners worked it from the early 1300s, and merchants from Ragusa ran the trade, shipping silver mixed with gold to Venice and beyond. The silver paid for the courts and monasteries of the Serbian kings and despots. The Ottomans besieged it in 1455 under Mehmed II, killed or enslaved much of the population, and kept the mines working on a smaller scale. Its fall marked the end of medieval Serbia's wealth.
sum: Novo Brdo is a hill town in eastern Kosovo whose mines made it the biggest source of silver in the Balkans in the 1300s and 1400s. Its fortress ruins still stand above the village.
